newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Rouble stable on quarter-end fund reserving.
newsitem.headline: Rouble stable on quarter-end fund reserving.

text.p: The rouble was steady in lively trading on Wednesday ahead of the quarter-end, with banks seeking funds to square their books and meet compulsory reserve requirements at the central bank, dealers said.
"The quarter-end is close and the rouble is in the middle of the central bank (bid/offer) rates," a European Trade Bank dealer said.
The rouble generally trades at the lower end of the bid/offer range set daily by the central bank since mid-May for its deals with major Russian banks.
Menatep Bank dealer Mikhail Zaretsky said rates had been fluctuating in a narrow 10-point range on banks' mixed arbitrage and client interests.
"Fluctuations are not big but anyway it is more interesting than the dollar standing at the upper limit of the central bank's rates," he said.
Dealers said dollar demand was likely to rise after banks set aside quarter-end funds.

Roubles for today settlement were quoted at 5,388-90 per dollar compared with an early 5,394-97 and 5,393-96 late on Tuesday. Tomorrow roubles edged up to 5,397-99 per dollar from yesterday's late 5,399-5,401.
The central bank said it had set 5,372/5,412 as its bid and offer rates against the dollar on Wednesday.
Overnight rouble credits yielded 60-80 percent compared with Tuesday's late 5-10 percent.
